title: A Different Perspective
paragraphs: “That sounds just like you, Naofumi-san.”
“Really? When it comes to reading people, Ren is probably more perceptive—Ah, wait, maybe not.”
“What do you mean by that, bringing me into the conversation just to deny it?”
Ren, looking slightly displeased, joined the discussion.
“No offense intended. I just thought you’d be harder to fool, but that’s a different issue.”
“Go on, explain.”
“Ren is always wary of others. Rather than trusting people from the start, you keep your guard up… There’s a kind of wall between you and others.”

“If I had to put it in a scenario, say you see someone being attacked by a monster right in front of you. Instead of acting on instinct, your rational mind would start analyzing multiple possibilities, making it harder for you to move immediately.”
“Like assuming they might be faking it? Or thinking the monster is actually a tamed creature just playing around?”
“Exactly.”
That actually makes a lot of sense. Ren is highly cautious of others. In fact, in all the previous loops, he has always kept his distance from Melromarc. Father nodded at Itsuki’s response.

“In that sense, when it comes to dealing with people, you should probably use Ren as a reference. Even in situations where trust is necessary, he still explores every possibility. If someone starts acting strangely, he gathers evidence and lets his doubts grow. That way, in the end, he gets deceived far less often.”
“I see. That was very insightful. Ren-san, I’ll be learning from you.”
“Stop making me into some kind of example!”
Father and Itsuki were teasing Ren.
“In situations like earlier, in the end, all you can do is gather evidence. Aside from that… ’When in Rome, do as the Romans do’… I suppose.”
“You mean… accepting bribes as bribes?”
“I guess so. Here, giving bribes—what we’d call tipping in foreign countries—is just common sense. We’re applying Japanese values too rigidly.”
It’s like traveling abroad. I’ve been on overseas trips many times myself.
“I heard that in some countries, hotel staff don’t have hourly wages, and they rely on tips for their income!”
“Yeah, I’ve heard the same thing, Motoyasu-kun. It’s kind of like that. But at the end of the day, if someone is in trouble, you listen to them and help in any way you can. It’s just goodwill.”
“Goodwill…?”

“Yeah. Goodwill and justice are different things, though. If someone is in trouble, you help them. But if there’s both a person in trouble and a person causing the trouble, then you listen to both sides… Ideally. But that’s not always easy.”
“I agree.”

“There’s no absolute right answer. There’s even a saying, ‘History is written by the victors.’ Some problems can only be solved with power. This is another world, after all… But still, constantly questioning yourself about whether you’re truly right—that might be the most just thing of all.”
“In novels, there are those pathetic protagonists who keep brooding over things forever… Is it like that?”

“A protagonist who pushes forward with conviction is cool, but some cross the line and commit crimes without hesitation. From what Motoyasu-kun told me, I feel like that’s what happened to Itsuki—he followed his own sense of justice without question, and that was the result.”
“Hmm. When portrayed as an ally, they seem righteous, but if they were the enemy, they’d be seen in a completely different light.”

Ren nodded at Father’s words. That makes sense. I fought against Itsuki many times, and he never wavered—he simply labeled me and Father as evil and refused to even consider otherwise. Back then, I thought he was just a pain, but in a way, he was decisive and proactive.
“Well, Motoyasu-kun, you’re a prime example of that too.”
“W-Well… you’re not wrong…”

“Right now, Itsuki is constantly questioning himself, right? Wondering which path is truly right. If he keeps struggling and eventually finds an answer, then even after making his choice, if he continues to reflect on it and consider if there was a better option… perhaps that kind of justice, born from experience and self-doubt, is more valuable. But coming from someone like me, who lacks experience, that probably doesn’t sound too convincing.”
“…No, that was a really insightful perspective. Naofumi-san, Ren-san, thank you.”
Itsuki seemed to have shaken off some of his doubts. …Huh? Nothing for me?
“I personally prefer situations like Naofumi-san’s, where it’s easy to tell who’s in the wrong.”
“Haha… yeah, in that situation, from a Japanese perspective, I was just a poor victim.”
“But… in Melromarc, setting up Naofumi was considered justice. Since the Shield Hero—the ‘devil’—is an enemy in their religion, they believe anything done to him is justified.”
“Oh? That reminds me, someone once told Itsuki in the first world, ‘The opposite of justice is another justice.’ I just remembered that now.”
“I don’t know whose words those were.”
“It feels like something the villagers said…”

Since my sources of information were the Filolials and a few of the slaves, my knowledge is quite muddled. And because I didn’t hear those words directly, I can’t recall exactly. So identifying who said them would be difficult.
“That person must truly understand the meaning of justice. Yes… When you lose, your justice is condemned as evil. I see now.”
“So, Itsuki, what do you want to do?”
Father looked at Itsuki with concern before shifting his gaze to the townscape.

“Nothing in particular… We just do what we can. I have you, Naofumi-san, Motoyasu-san, and Ren-san with me. If I stray from the right path, I have friends who will correct me. As long as I keep moving forward, even with doubts, that’s enough.”
“W-Well, that’s some pressure.”
“Yeah. There’s always a chance we could all be wrong together.”
“But I feel like the chances of making mistakes drop significantly. Naofumi-san, I’ve chosen to trust you, so at least cooperate with me.”
“I see… That’s true. Back then, you believed I wasn’t guilty. So I’ll help as much as I can.”
After getting Father’s agreement, Itsuki nodded deeply.
“Now that the discussion is settled, I have a job request from the guild for you heroes.”
“Oh?”
Éclair held out a stack of request papers. She had great timing. She was probably waiting for the right moment.
“I believe the current group of heroes can handle this. It’s a task that should be completed quickly.”
“What kind of job?”
“A request to exterminate a swarm of monsters that have been causing trouble. How about taking it on as part of your training?”
“Sounds good.”
“However…”
Itsuki and Ren looked at me.
What’s with that look? If it’s just monster extermination, I can clear it up in a few hours. I spun my spear around confidently.
“Kitamura-dono, please restrain yourself.”
“Why?”
“Because it won’t serve as training for the other heroes.”
“That’s nonsense! Well, anyway, let’s ride on Sakura-chan and get the job done.”
At Father’s words, Sakura-chan, Yuki-chan, and the others’ eyes sparkled with excitement.
“Are we going?”
“Yeah. This will be a good opportunity for the heroes to practice teamwork.”
“We won’t gain experience points, but we’ll gain a different kind of experience.”
“That’s right. And for me, it’ll be good practice fighting alongside people other than Kou-san and Eclair-san.”
“I’ll make sure to hold back as much as I can!”
For some reason, Father and the others gave me exasperated looks before climbing into the carriage. I’m getting fired up. Time to practice holding back.
“Alright, let’s head out!”
“Yes, let’s go!”
And so, following the request details Éclair had brought, we set out on a monster extermination mission.
